title: DA3408 A4 · CPU Image Captioning – Application & Host Monitoring
description: Streamlit + BLIP captioning app instrumented with prometheus_client, correlated with node_exporter host metrics. AI attribution: generated with Claude (Anthropic) from the prompt "give the remaining required files for node exporter, prometheus.yaml and grafana dashboard"; every query is explained in PROMQL.md.

panels.title: How to read this dashboard

options.content:
**CPU image-captioning service: health → performance → system correlation → workload → clients → runtime.** Read top to bottom: if a stat in row 1 is not blue, drill into the rows below.  
Colours use the colour-blind-safe Okabe-Ito palette, and within a graph each series also has its own line style (solid / dashed / dotted) with point markers, so plots stay readable in greyscale print or PDF. Purple shaded regions on every graph mark when a **bulk ZIP batch** was running, so app spikes can be matched against CPU / RAM / disk. Hover the ⓘ on any panel for its story. Every graph states its y-axis units and scale (linear or log₁₀); the x-axis is always wall-clock time.

panels.title: 1 · Service health (now)
App status · /metrics scrape
panels.description: UP when Prometheus' latest scrape of the Streamlit app's /metrics endpoint (port 8000) succeeded. DOWN means the app process is not running or not reachable.

panels.title: Node exporter · host metrics
panels.description: UP when node_exporter (port 9100) is being scraped. Without it the system-resource rows below go blank.

panels.title: Model · BLIP in memory
panels.description: LOADED once the first session has loaded the captioning model into RAM (it is cached for all later sessions).

panels.title: App uptime · since process start
panels.description: Time since the Streamlit process started. A sudden drop to ~0 means the app restarted (counters reset).

panels.title: Active requests · being processed now
panels.description: Requests currently inside the app (a Single caption click or a whole Bulk batch). Orange from 2, vermillion from 4: concurrent work on a CPU-only model queues up and inflates latency.

panels.title: Images captioned · in selected time range
panels.description: How many images were captioned successfully (both modes) within the dashboard's time range.

panels.title: Image error ratio · in selected time range
panels.description: Share of images that failed (corrupt file, decode or inference error) out of all images handled in the range. Orange above 5%, vermillion above 10%.

panels.title: Firing alerts · Prometheus rules
panels.description: Number of alert rules currently firing (see http://localhost:9090/alerts for which ones).

panels.title: 2 · Throughput & latency (application)
Throughput · images captioned per second, by mode
panels.description:
How fast the service is producing captions. Single-mode traffic shows as short blips; a bulk ZIP shows as a sustained plateau whose height is the CPU's sustainable captioning rate. The dotted vermillion line counts images that failed or were skipped.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Images per second (linear).

panels.title: Inference latency · p50 / p95 / p99 per image
panels.description:
Time spent in `model.generate()` per image. p50 is the typical image, p99 the slowest 1%. The gap between them widens when the CPU is contended (e.g. a bulk batch running while someone uses Single mode). Log scale so sub-second and multi-second values are both readable.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Latency per image (seconds, log₁₀ scale).

panels.title: Request duration · mean end-to-end time (Summary)
panels.description:
Average wall time of a whole user request: one image for Single mode, the entire ZIP for Bulk mode. Bulk sits orders of magnitude higher because it covers many images, hence the log scale.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Mean request time (seconds, log₁₀ scale).

panels.title: Pipeline breakdown · mean seconds per stage, per image
panels.description:
Where an image's time goes: decoding bytes, BLIP preprocessing (resize + normalise) and model inference. Inference dominates by ~2 orders of magnitude, so optimisation effort belongs there. Log scale.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Mean time per image (seconds, log₁₀ scale).

custom.axisLabel: Mean time per image (seconds, log₁₀ scale)

panels.title: Latency distribution · inference-time heatmap
panels.description:
Each column is a time slice; each row a latency bucket; colour = how many images landed in that bucket (Cividis scale: dark = few, bright = many). Shows whether latency is a tight band or spread out, which percentiles alone hide.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y = inference-latency bucket upper bound (seconds).

panels.title: Errors · failures per minute, by pipeline stage
panels.description:
Failures split by where they happened: `zip` (bad archive), `decode` (corrupt / non-image file) or `inference` (model error). A rise in `decode` usually means a bad upload, not a broken service.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Errors per minute (linear).

panels.title: Requests by outcome · requests per second
panels.description:
User requests (one Single click or one Bulk batch) split by result. `partial` = a bulk batch where some images failed.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Requests per second (linear).

panels.title: 3 · App ↔ system correlation (node_exporter)
Host CPU busy · now
panels.description: Share of CPU time not idle, averaged over all cores. Expect it near 100% / (cores) × torch threads during bulk.

panels.title: Host RAM used · now
panels.description: Memory in use by everything on the host (not counting reclaimable cache). The BLIP model alone takes ~1.5-2 GB.

panels.title: Root disk used · now
panels.description: How full the root filesystem is. The model cache (~1 GB) and Prometheus' TSDB live here.

panels.title: Load vs work · run-queue length and inferences in flight
panels.description:
1-minute load average against the number of CPU cores (dashed grey). When a bulk batch runs, load climbs towards the core count while exactly one inference is in flight: the model is using several cores per image.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Runnable tasks (linear). Y (right) = inferences in flight (count).

panels.title: CPU vs bulk throughput · does load follow the work?
panels.description:
The key correlation plot. Host CPU % (solid) and the app process' own CPU % (dashed) on the left axis, bulk captioning rate (dotted, right axis). During a ZIP batch all three rise together; the app line sitting just under the host line shows the spike is the captioning app, not something else on the machine.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = CPU busy (% of all cores, linear). Y (right) = bulk images per second.

custom.axisLabel: CPU busy (% of all cores, linear)

panels.title: Memory vs queue · host RAM, app RSS and images waiting
panels.description:
Host memory in use (solid) and the app's resident memory (dashed, mostly the BLIP weights) on the left axis; images still waiting in running bulk batches (dotted, right axis). RSS jumps once when the model loads and then stays flat, so memory is not what scales with batch size; CPU time is.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Memory (bytes, linear). Y (right) = images queued (count).

panels.title: Disk & upload I/O · bytes per second
panels.description:
Disk reads/writes (all block devices) next to the bytes users upload into the app. The first model load is a large disk-read burst; ZIP uploads appear as upload spikes.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Throughput (bytes per second, linear).

panels.title: App process · OS threads vs torch intra-op threads
panels.description:
Threads in the Streamlit process versus the threads torch may use for matrix maths. Torch is capped at (cores − 1) so the UI thread stays responsive.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Threads (count, linear).

panels.title: 4 · Workload characteristics
Work in flight · queued images and active requests
panels.description:
Bulk images not yet captioned (dotted) and requests being processed, by mode. A queue that drains at a steady slope shows healthy batch progress; a flat non-zero queue fires the BulkQueueStuck alert.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Count (linear).

panels.title: Input images · file size and resolution (p50 / p95)
panels.description:
What users are uploading. File size (left, log scale) and megapixels (right). BLIP resizes everything to 384×384, so resolution mainly affects decode time, not inference time.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = File size (bytes, log₁₀ scale). Y (right) = megapixels (linear).

panels.title: Caption length · mean tokens and characters
panels.description:
How long the generated captions are. Tokens come from the histogram, characters from the Summary. A sudden change would hint at a model or preprocessing change.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Tokens per caption (linear). Y (right) = characters per caption.

panels.title: Bulk batches · size and duration of the latest batch
panels.description:
Images in the most recent ZIP (solid, left) and how long it took (dashed, right). Their ratio is the per-image cost: roughly linear means the CPU is the only bottleneck.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Images in batch (count, linear). Y (right) = batch duration (seconds).

panels.title: Upload hygiene · ZIP uploads and skipped files (time range)
panels.description: ZIP archives by validity and files the bulk mode refused to caption, by reason, within the selected time range. Each bar is labelled, so no legend is needed. Unit: count of files / archives.

panels.title: 5 · Clients (custom labels: session, IP, browser)
Per-client activity · requests per session (time range)
panels.description: One row per browser session: its client IP, browser, mode and outcome, with the number of requests made in the selected range. Sort or filter the columns to find a heavy user.

targets.expr: round(sum by (session_id, client_ip, browser, mode, status) (increase(caption_requests_total[$__range]))) > 0

panels.title: Traffic by browser · requests per second
panels.description:
Which browsers the requests come from (parsed from the User-Agent header).

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Requests per second (linear).

panels.title: Distinct sessions · since app start
panels.description: Browser sessions that have opened the app since it last restarted.

panels.title: 6 · Runtime & monitoring health
Build info · model and library versions
panels.description: Static metadata exported once at model load: model name, device, torch / transformers / Python versions, OS.

panels.title: Model parameters · BLIP base
panels.description: Number of weights in the loaded model (~247 M for BLIP-base).

panels.title: Model load time · cold start
panels.description: How long `from_pretrained` took. Much longer on the very first run, when the weights are downloaded.

panels.title: Total uploaded · since app start
panels.description: All bytes users have uploaded (images + ZIPs) since the app started.

panels.title: Scrape health · time to scrape each target
panels.description:
How long Prometheus takes to collect each target (solid lines, left) and how many samples it got from the app (dotted, right). Scrapes must finish well under the 5 s interval; samples grow as new label sets appear.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Scrape duration (seconds, log₁₀ scale). Y (right) = samples per scrape.

panels.title: Tokens generated · caption tokens per second, by mode
panels.description:
Output volume of the model. Together with throughput this gives tokens per image.

Axes: X = wall-clock time. Y (left) = Tokens per second (linear).
